title: ClipCraft public beta
summary: The first ClipCraft beta brings together screenshot capture, an editable annotation workspace, reusable templates and multipage guides, with an unsigned Windows installer alongside portable and source downloads.

Capture and startup: Capture Controller opens by default for new profiles; existing preferences are preserved and development badges default off.
Print Screen captures with saved settings; Alt+F11 captures a region. Print Screen conflicts have a fallback, while other registered shortcuts remain available.
Separate Editor and Capture Controller Start menu entries use crisp, distinct icons. The first-launch controller icon correction was confirmed by the maintainer.
Frames and multipage guides: Convert shapes to image frames and back; retain outline/shape geometry while choosing images from files, clipboard or Library. External image drops highlight the receiving frame.
Horizontal guide pages support add, duplicate, delete and reorder. Page and section hierarchy appears in Objects, with section drag/reorder and cross-page movement.
Separated page control strips, aligned section actions, scaled/clipped Choose Image controls and clearer add/delete icons.
Page Setup and editing: Page Setup includes page presets, dimensions in pixels/inches/cm, resolution, orientation, margins, headers/footers, numbering, bleed and crop marks. Per-page geometry is honored in PDF/print output.
The Advanced ribbon replaces the former settings ribbons, with a prominent Page Setup control and Restore section.
Raster/frame rendering reuse, outline bounds, dynamic scrollbars, fixed preview layout, consistent confirmation actions and connector quick-style variations.
Distribution and verification: Unsigned per-user installer with separate shortcuts, portable ZIP and complete buildable Apache-2.0 source. Setup preserves Library/settings data on removal.

649 Rust tests plus formatting/strict Clippy; 51 optimized image comparisons and nine independent PDF page comparisons were recorded for the preceding application candidate. The release workflow reruns the Rust and packaging checks for the exact tagged source.
Installer lifecycle checks run on a fresh Windows build runner, without starting the capture app. Downloads include checksums, source manifest, SPDX inventory and GitHub provenance attestations.
Public documentation now describes ClipCraft directly, while preserving required third-party attribution and historical binary archives.

limitations: Beta software; installer and binaries are unsigned. MSI/all-user deployment, signing and an in-app updater are not included.
Video and All-in-One capture, mixed formatting in one text box, and general SVG/EPS stamp import remain future work.
Known deferred cosmetic issue: on some multi-monitor setups the right border moves inward while inactive and recovers on focus.

Automated tests do not replace broader Windows desktop testing. Recent page-control/quick-style/stamp-overlay behavior, high-zoom interaction across hardware and physical printer output still need wider beta feedback.
PDF text uses vector outlines and is not searchable. Images and pixel effects remain raster; editable project fonts are referenced rather than embedded.
Editable projects retain source pixels. Share flattened exports when redacting; do not share editable source documents containing confidential content.
Projects using the new page setup/layout use format 30 and require a compatible new release. Keep backups before updating; earlier releases may reject newer projects.
This is a bounded maintainer review, not an independent security or legal certification.
